mentions.name: pglockanalyze
mentions.description: A CLI tool that makes reasoning about Postgres locks easier. Given a database (typically an ephemeral one spawned by a CI pipeline) and a set of DDL statements or migrations, it opens a transaction, executes the statements, reads the pg_locks view to analyze the locks they acquire, rolls back or commits the transaction depending on flags, and outputs results for each statement. It acts as a complement, not a replacement, to static analysis and the official Postgres docs.
mentions.problem: Reasoning about the locks acquired by Postgres DDL statements and migrations is difficult; static analysis and documentation alone don't show what locks statements actually take.
mentions.source_excerpt:
A CLI tool to make reasoning about Postgres locks a bit easier.

Given a database[1] and a set of DDL statements/migrations you want to check, pglockanalyze will open a transaction, execute the statements, read the pg_locks view to analyze the locks they acquire and rollback (or commit, depending on the flags you passed) the transaction.
